discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the LHC and its general-purpose detectors ATLAS and CMS
motivation: The 2013 prize honoured the theoretical prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, but the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 remains unrecognised. It was made possible by an unprecedented accelerator and two independent detectors designed specifically to find it. Lyn Evans led the design and construction of the Large Hadron Collider. Peter Jenni and Michel Della Negra conceived and led ATLAS and CMS from the earliest proto-collaborations, through detector concepts able to resolve H→γγ and H→ZZ→4ℓ, to commissioning. Their choices on calorimetry, tracking and muon systems enabled the 5σ observation and the precision programme that followed: couplings, spin-parity, and now the first constraints on Higgs pair production and the self-coupling, which bear on the shape of the Higgs potential and the electroweak phase transition. This is a definite discovery about nature's fundamental structure, won through decades of instrumental vision.
